questions.question: Explain how AI-based systems can improve agricultural productivity / through crop monitoring, disease detection and resource management.
questions.solution_html:
• .AI improves agricultural productivity by analyzing data collected from sensors, drones
  • satellites, and cameras.
  • ● Crop monitoring: AI analyzes images and sensor data to monitor crop growth, soil
  • conditions, and plant health.
  • ● Disease detection: Machine-learning algorithms and image processing identify
  • symptoms of plant diseases and pest attacks at an early stage.
  • ● Precision irrigation: AI determines the water requirements of crops using soil moisture
  • weather, and crop data.
  • ● Resource management: AI helps optimize the use of fertilizers, pesticides, water, and
  • agricultural machinery.
  • ● Yield prediction: AI analyzes weather conditions, soil characteristics, and historical crop
  • data to estimate crop yields.
  • Thus, AI supports timely decisions, reduces resource wastage, lowers production costs
  • and improves agricultural productivity.

questions.question: Explain the relationship between expert knowledge and problem solving / in an Expert System.
questions.solution_html:
• .Expert knowledge is the specialized knowledge acquired from human experts through
  • experience, training, and practice. In an expert system, this knowledge is represented as
  • facts, rules, and heuristics in a knowledge base.
  • The inference engine applies logical rules to the available facts to derive conclusions
  • and recommend solutions. It may use forward chaining, which begins with known facts
  • or backward chaining, which works backward from a goal.
  • For example, a medical expert system may use symptoms and diagnostic rules to
  • suggest possible diseases. The accuracy of its recommendations depends on the
  • quality, completeness, and reliability of the knowledge base. Therefore, expert
  • knowledge enables an expert system to solve domain-specific problems and support
  • decision-making.

questions.question: Discuss how Expert Systems can support decision-making in / Environmental Management.
questions.solution_html:
• Expert systems support environmental management by applying stored environmental
  • knowledge and rules to analyze data and recommend appropriate actions
  • ● Pollution control: Identify possible sources of air, water, and soil pollution.
  • ● Environmental risk assessment: Evaluate potential environmental hazards and their
  • consequences.
  • ● Waste management: Recommend appropriate methods for waste treatment, disposal
  • and recycling.
  • ● Resource conservation: Suggest measures for efficient use of water, energy, and other
  • natural resources.
  • ● Regulatory compliance: Help assess whether environmental practices conform to
  • applicable standards and regulations.
  • ● For example, an expert system can analyze water-quality measurements and
  • expert-defined rules to identify possible contamination and recommend further
  • investigation or treatment. However, its effectiveness depends on the reliability of the
  • data and the knowledge base.

questions.question: Explain the suitability of Generate and Test, Breadth-First Search, and / Depth-First.
questions.solution_html:
• Generate-and-Test: This method generates possible solutions and tests each candidate
  • against the required conditions. It is suitable when candidate solutions can be generated
  • and evaluated easily. For example, it can be used to test possible arrangements in a
  • puzzle.
  • ● Breadth-First Search (BFS): BFS explores nodes level by level, visiting all nodes at one
  • depth before proceeding to the next. It is suitable for finding a shortest path in an
  • unweighted graph. However, it may require considerable memory when the branching
  • factor is large.
  • ● Depth-First Search (DFS): DFS explores one branch as deeply as possible before
  • backtracking to other branches. It is suitable for problems with limited memory
  • requirements and where solutions may occur deep in the search tree. However, it may
  • become trapped in an infinite path unless depth limits or cycle detection are used.
  • ● Thus, Generate-and-Test is appropriate for straightforward candidate checking, BFS for
  • shallowest-solution search, and DFS for memory-efficient deep exploration.
questions.final_answer: shallowest-solution search, and DFS for memory-efficient deep exploration

questions.question: Differentiate local heuristic and global heuristic using a suitable search- / tree example.
questions.solution_html:
• .A local heuristic evaluates the immediate state or neighbouring nodes to select the next
  • move. It focuses on the local situation and may not consider the overall cost of reaching
  • the goal.
  • A global heuristic considers the broader search problem and estimates how promising a
  • state is in relation to the overall goal or remaining path cost.
  • ● Consider the following search tree
  • ● S
  • ● / \
  • ● A B
  • ● / \ / \
  • ● C D E G*
  • ● Suppose the search begins at S and the goal is G.
  • ● A local heuristic may select A because it appears promising based on its immediate
  • characteristics, even though it does not lead directly to the goal. A global, goal-directed
  • heuristic may favour B because its descendants include G, the goal state.
  • ● Therefore, local heuristics can guide immediate decisions, whereas global or
  • goal-directed heuristic evaluation can help guide search toward the overall solution. The
  • effectiveness of either approach depends on how accurately the heuristic estimates the
  • problem's structure.

questions.question: Explain how inheritance works in a category hierarchy and how it helps / in knowledge inference.
questions.solution_html:
• Inheritance is a knowledge-representation mechanism in which a subclass or individual
  • obtains properties from a more general category in a hierarchy.
  • For example
  • ● Animal is a general category.
  • ● Bird is a subclass of Animal.
  • ● Sparrow is a subclass of Bird.
  • ● Birds generally have wings and feathers.
  • If a sparrow belongs to the category Bird, it inherits the properties associated with
  • birds. Since Bird is a subclass of Animal, the sparrow also inherits applicable
  • properties of animals.
  • Inheritance reduces the need to store the same properties repeatedly and supports
  • efficient knowledge inference. An AI system can derive new facts from existing
  • category relationships. In systems that support default reasoning, exceptions can also
  • be represented, such as the fact that not every bird can fly.
questions.final_answer: be represented, such as the fact that not every bird can fly

questions.question: Differentiate local heuristic and global heuristic using a suitable search- / tree example.
questions.solution_html:
• .A local heuristic evaluates the immediate state or neighbouring nodes to select the next
  • move. It focuses on the local situation and may not consider the overall cost of reaching
  • the goal.
  • A global heuristic considers the broader search problem and estimates how promising a
  • state is in relation to the overall goal or remaining path cost.
  • ● Consider the following search tree
  • ● S
  • ● / \
  • ● A B
  • ● / \ / \
  • ● C D E G*
  • ● Suppose the search begins at S and the goal is G.
  • ● A local heuristic may select A because it appears promising based on its immediate
  • characteristics, even though it does not lead directly to the goal. A global, goal-directed
  • heuristic may favour B because its descendants include G, the goal state.
  • ● Therefore, local heuristics can guide immediate decisions, whereas global or
  • goal-directed heuristic evaluation can help guide search toward the overall solution. The
  • effectiveness of either approach depends on how accurately the heuristic estimates the
  • problem's structure.

questions.question: Explain how inheritance works in a category hierarchy and how it helps / in knowledge inference.
questions.solution_html:
• Inheritance is a knowledge-representation mechanism in which a subclass or individual
  • obtains properties from a more general category in a hierarchy.
  • For example
  • ● Animal is a general category.
  • ● Bird is a subclass of Animal.
  • ● Sparrow is a subclass of Bird.
  • ● Birds generally have wings and feathers.
  • If a sparrow belongs to the category Bird, it inherits the properties associated with
  • birds. Since Bird is a subclass of Animal, the sparrow also inherits applicable
  • properties of animals.
  • Inheritance reduces the need to store the same properties repeatedly and supports
  • efficient knowledge inference. An AI system can derive new facts from existing
  • category relationships. In systems that support default reasoning, exceptions can also
  • be represented, such as the fact that not every bird can fly.
questions.final_answer: be represented, such as the fact that not every bird can fly
